narrative: This daily brief highlights significant advancements across technology, AI, infrastructure, science, and developer communities. Key themes include new open-source AI tools, important developments in AI hardware and policy, and ongoing progress in space exploration and research ethics.

highlights.title: Mozilla to UK regulators: VPNs are essential privacy and security tools
highlights.whyItMatters: Mozilla advocates for VPNs as crucial for user privacy and security against potential government interference.

highlights.title: Zerostack – A Unix-inspired coding agent written in pure Rust
highlights.whyItMatters: A new open-source coding agent built in Rust offers Unix-inspired features for developers.

highlights.title: OpenAI and Government of Malta partner to roll out ChatGPT Plus to all citizens
highlights.whyItMatters: Malta becomes the first country to provide ChatGPT Plus access to all its citizens through a partnership with OpenAI.

highlights.title: $60B AI chip darling Cerebras almost died early on, burning $8M a month
highlights.whyItMatters: Cerebras Systems, a significant AI chip company, faced severe financial challenges in its early stages before achieving its current valuation.

highlights.title: SANA-WM, a 2.6B open-source world model for 1-minute 720p video
highlights.whyItMatters: SANA-WM is introduced as a large open-source world model capable of generating one-minute 720p videos.

highlights.title: The US is betting on AI to catch insider trading in prediction markets
highlights.whyItMatters: The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission is employing AI to detect insider trading activities within prediction markets.

highlights.title: Musk v. Altman week 3: Elon Musk and Sam Altman traded blows over each other’s credibility. Now the jury will pick a side.
highlights.whyItMatters: The intense legal battle between Elon Musk and Sam Altman continues, with the jury poised to decide on their credibility.

highlights.title: NASA Science, Cargo Launch on 34th SpaceX Resupply Mission to Station
highlights.whyItMatters: SpaceX successfully launched its 34th resupply mission, delivering new scientific experiments and cargo to the International Space Station.
